headline: Stochastic gene regulatory networks link expression noise to differentiation landscapes
label: Stochastic Gene Regulatory Dynamics
summary: Recent preprints apply explicit stochastic network models to cell-state heterogeneity, population renewal, and large-scale GPU-based network optimization.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of explicit gene regulatory network models to connect stochastic expression with cell-state heterogeneity and differentiation. The unified PDE-integral framework (arXiv:2611.19257) couples stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics with population renewal to define a dynamic Waddington landscape. The jaxgrn framework (arXiv:2611.20172) applies differentiable programming to optimize thousands of gene regulatory networks end-to-end on GPUs using stochastic simulation. The bioRxiv preprint (10.64898/2026.11.18.767571) examines network topology directly, reporting that positive-cycle tangles and mutual inhibition enable hierarchical differentiation patterns in simulated dynamic GRN models. What is new is the joint treatment of population-level renewal, landscape geometry, and large-scale network optimization, although all three items are preprints and remain unreviewed.
